column1: # Persian (Standard), ISIRI 9147 (kbdfar.dll)
# Source: the Windows keyboard layout 00050429 ("Persian (Standard)"), read from the operating system with
# dump.ps1 (Win32 ToUnicodeEx on the layout, Windows Server 2025 build 26100, 2026-11-09).
# It is data, not a table typed from memory: every later change of it is a diff a reader can
# compare with a fresh run of dump.ps1. The generator (gen/main.go) turns it into
# ../layouts_gen.go, and TestLayoutTablesAreGenerated fails if that file drifts.
# Columns, tab separated: scan code (hex), then four code point lists ("U+0041+U+0042" is
# two characters): the key on the US layout (00000409) unshifted and shifted, and the key on
# this layout unshifted and shifted. An empty cell is a key with no character. The US legend
# is what a Persian letter is "read as" (4.3): the key it shares with a Latin letter.
# One cell is the standard's and not the system's (P1 auth review round 9, primitives-r9-1): scan code 2D,
# Shift+X. ToUnicodeEx on kbdfar.dll (Windows Server 2025 build 26100) reports tah (U+0637) there, which is the
# unshifted letter again; ISIRI 9147 puts the combining maddah above (U+0653) on that key, and the systems that
# implement the standard (Linux, macOS, Android) type it, so a shifted walk Shift+Z, Shift+X, Shift+C arrives as
# U+0643 U+0653 U+0698 and must read as "zxc". A fresh run of dump.ps1 therefore differs from this file in ONE
# row, this one, and that is expected. The other cells of the shifted bottom row (Z U+0643, C U+0698, V U+0670,
# B U+200C, N U+0654, M U+0621) agree with the standard, which is why the dump is otherwise trusted; the test
# TestLayoutDataShowsTheFactsOfSpec43 pins the whole shifted row.
# Two more cells are the standard's and not the system's (round 10, primitives-r10-8): scan code 29, Shift+`
# (the division sign U+00F7; the dump reports the unshifted ZWJ there again, the same fault as Shift+X) and
# scan code 05, Shift+4 (the rial sign U+FDFC; the dump shows its NFKC form, the four letters of "rial", which
# no key types). Both were read from the published standard (Wikipedia, "Persian keyboard layout") and are
# pinned by TestLayoutDataShowsTheFactsOfSpec43. The generator enters U+FDFC under its own code point and
# pwstrength reads a typed character before it applies NFKC, so the rial sign reads as the key "4".
# A fresh run of dump.ps1 therefore differs from this file in THREE rows (2D, 29, 05), and that is expected.
